pool.text: The Comité Spécial du Katanga was established as a semi-private concessionary company.
The Belgian government established the modern-day government in the city of Élisabethville.
The whites-only Ligue de Football du Katanga was founded in Elisabethville.
The first official local football championship called the B was organized in Elisabethville.
Belgian colonial authorities experimented with self-governance by establishing the cité indigène of Élisabethville.
The first indigenous chief, Albert Kabongo, was appointed in Élisabethville.
Miners in Élisabethville conducted a strike in December to protest the forced-labour regime.
Albert Kabongo, the first indigenous chief of Élisabethville, was dismissed from his post.
The black Elisabethville Football Association had over thirty affiliated clubs competing in leagues.
There were eight thousand black homeowners and many skilled workers in the city.
The Belgians established the University of Élisabethville, now known as the University of Lubumbashi.
Moise Tshombe proclaimed Katangan independence in July during the Congolese civil war.
Congolese leaders arrested Moise Tshombe and charged him with treason in April.
United Nations troops opposed Katangan forces and took control of the city in December.
Moise Tshombe renamed Élisabethville to Lubumbashi.
Katanga was renamed to Shaba by the authorities.
Zenith Radio started broadcasting as the first independent radio station in the city.
Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo rebels captured Lubumbashi in April.
Laurent-Désiré Kabila declared himself president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from Lubumbashi.
Great animals had been acquired for the zoo by this year.
